title: Capacity credit timestep — headcount migration playbook (2026)
description: Working spreadsheet-style playbook for migrating engineering headcount across capacity credit buckets over 4-week timesteps, and quantifying pricing/headcount sensitivity under slab vs burst commitments.
summary: This is a tactical workbook to simulate moving X FTEs between Reserved / Shared / On-demand pools across 6 timesteps (4-week windows). Goal: contain 90-day burn, keep latency SLO for hosted API routes, and evaluate price-impact under three pricing experiments (flat slab, micro-banded, surge-credit).
key_assumptions: Base monthly payroll per FE-equivalent = $15,200 (fully loaded)
GPU cost proxy per reserved unit = $9,000/mo; burst spot equivalent = $3,800/mo (avg)
Average token mix: 55% chat gen, 30% embedding, 15% reranking — affects throughput util
Quantization adopton reduces cost per token by 18% after timestep 2 for eligible routes
Compliance/on-prem delta: 12% incremental infra + 1.3x hiring premium for SRE/ops roles
headcount_phases: T0 (weeks 0–4): baseline 148 engineers; 42 in serving-runtime & infra; 18 SRE; 12 solutions/prof svc
T1 (weeks 5–8): shift 8 backend ICs from on-demand to dedicated-support pool to stabilize latency — add 2 contractors for burst
T2 (weeks 9–12): experiment quantization pilot — move 4 model infra hires from hiring freeze into pilot team; defer 6 generalist hires
T3 (weeks 13–16): apply role-swap plan if price delta > 12%: reclass 3 senior infra -> contractor FTEs, release 2 junior backend roles
T4 (weeks 17–20): compliance window — earmark 6 headcount for Private/VPC onboarding; apply 1.12x cost uplift for those roles
T5 (weeks 21–24): steady-state rebalancing: target 140 engineers, reserve buffer of 6 contractors for microburst
budget_line_items: Payroll: headcount-run-rate by role (engineer/sre/product/solutions) — monthly totals and cumulative 6-timestep run
Infra: reserved GPU commitments, spot/ondemand rental, regional replication overhead
Tools: observability retention increase for rollout period (extra $18k/mo for 2 months)
Compliance overhead: audit, KMS/HSM, legal review fees (one-time $120k + $8k/mo ops)
Contractor pool: contingency funding for 10% surge capacity
Credits: internal capacity credits allocation and account-level slab discounts applied per timestep
sensitivity_tests: Price experiment A — flat slab: 20% slab discount for committed reserved capacity; headcount migration cost vs baseline
Price experiment B — micro-banded: per-route microcommit tiers (low/med/high) with stepped discounts; measure churn in dedicated pool
Price experiment C — surge-credit: small prepaid credit pool to absorb 30% peak bursts; reduces sustained reserved commit by 8%
Stress test 1: 30% token demand spike in T2 — forced fallback to on-demand region; compute incremental infra + SLA penalty exposure
Stress test 2: 10% pricing compression from cloud vendor leading to immediate 9% downward pressure on resale price — model headcount deferral triggers
Headcount sensitivity: cost per additional IC vs throughput delta — compute break-even at 0.6% latency improvement per FTE
quick_findings: Preliminary: micro-banded pricing yields best unit cost for heterogeneous route mix but increases ops complexity (approx +0.9 FTE ops burden)
Surge-credit reduces immediate capital outlay but pushes marginal unit-cost up if utilization < 42%
Quantization pilot (T2) shows 12–22% per-token cost variance by model family; adopt conservative 18% for planning
Allocating 4 FTEs to Private onboarding increases near-term burn but protects top 3 enterprise deals (NPV > $1.2M over 12 months)
open_questions: What is acceptable SLO degradation when shifting 6 engineers from shared to dedicated? Are product owners ok with 5–10ms tail impact?
How quickly can solutions-eng redeploy contractors for on-prem PoC work (lead time assumptions)?
If slab discount is renegotiated mid-timestep, do we retroactively reallocate credits or apply forward adjustments?
Contingency triggers: define exact thresholds (token growth %, price slide %) that force headcount hiring freeze
